channel.description: UN News - Global perspective Human stories | Migrants and Refugees

item.title: ‘I have not lost my dreams’: Refugee education funding cuts threaten millions
item.description: A teenage girl who fled war-torn Sudan for neighbouring Egypt and hopes to pursue a technology degree is an example of why countries must ensure that young refugees can continue to learn.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Malaysia: UN agency urges safeguards after refugees returned to Myanmar
item.description: The UN refugee agency, UNHCR, has voiced concern over Malaysia’s decision to return 1,476 people to Myanmar amid an ongoing civil war and a dire human rights and humanitarian situation.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Funding cuts put 8.3 million refugees at risk of losing vital assistance
item.description: Haji Mohammad Shafi spent 44 years in Pakistan before he was forced to leave. He sold everything he owned and returned to Afghanistan with his five children, arriving with almost nothing.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Rohingya refugees deserve a future beyond survival, not endless displacement
item.description: Nine years after the mass displacement of the Rohingya from Myanmar, their situation remains one of the world's most protracted and complex refugee crises, marked by years of persecution and uncertainty over the prospect of returning home.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Winter aid for Gaza, West Bank; Haiti food production; migrant deaths at sea; human rights funding
item.description: The UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) is seeking to raise $97.5 million to protect 540,000 children and their families in Gaza and the West Bank from harsh winter conditions in the coming months.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Money sent home by migrants nearly doubles in a decade
item.description: Migrants sent $728.6 billion home to families in low and middle-income countries in 2025, nearly double the amount recorded a decade earlier, according to a new report from the UN’s International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD).
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Surge in displacement following fighting in southwest Yemen
item.description: At least 46,000 people have been displaced since renewed fighting last week between Houthi rebels and pro-government forces in southwestern Yemen, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) reported on Friday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Migrant deaths climb sharply in 2026, new UN data shows
item.description: Severe weather, war, economic pressure and shifting policies reshaped migration journeys across multiple regions in the first four months of 2026, driving a surge in deaths, according to new data released on Wednesday by the International Organization for Migration (IOM).
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Forced online scams: IOM warns trafficking networks are booming
item.description: A job advert can hide a criminal network, and a single click can lead to a nightmare. Hundreds of thousands of people are trafficked every year on the promise of legitimate work abroad, only to be held captive and forced into online scam operations.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: 75 years later, the promise to protect refugees faces its greatest test
item.description: As the world marks the 75th anniversary of the Refugee Convention, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has launched a global campaign urging governments, organizations and individuals to renew their commitment to protecting people forced to flee war, violence and persecution.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN refugee agency reports 144 migrants dead or missing off Mauritanian coast
item.description: The UN’s refugee agency (UNHCR) reports that 144 migrants attempting to reach Europe are dead or missing due to a series of “tragic maritime incidents” off the coast of Mauritania last week.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Appeal for calm in Kashmir, women on the move, Ebola deaths mount, 12th anniversary of MH17
item.description: The UN human rights chief, Volker Türk, has appealed for calm in Pakistan-Administered Kashmir amid unrest ahead of regional elections.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: More than 500 people feared dead in double Myanmar shipwreck tragedy
item.description: There is growing concern for at least 500 people believed to have been aboard two boats that reportedly capsized off Myanmar’s coast in recent days.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: People continue to stand by refugees, Gen Z shows most empathy
item.description: Protection for refugees has been enshrined in international law for more than seven decades, but how much support is there today for those fleeing conflict and persecution?
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: For one young refugee in Uganda, basketball is more than a game
item.description: When 19-year-old Stephane Kulimushi looks around the basketball court in Kampala where he trains young refugees, he sees more than players.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World Refugee Day: UN calls for renewed commitment and solidarity
item.description: The UN High Commissioner for Refugees has called on the international community to strengthen support for the nearly 42 million people worldwide who have fled their home countries to escape conflict, violence or persecution.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Resettlement remains out of reach for millions of refugees
item.description: As millions of people continue to flee their countries due to war or persecution, UNHCR, the UN refugee agency, called on Tuesday for an urgent expansion of refugee resettlement programmes, warning that available places continue to fall short of global needs.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: State-supported safe houses in Haiti, EU pact strengthens refugee protection, demand for ‘critical minerals’ intensifies
item.description: Haiti has opened its first State-supported safe house for survivors of sexual violence with support from the UN, marking a significant step in responding to the growing crisis affecting women and girls.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Refugee numbers drop for first time in a decade, but millions remain trapped
item.description: Global forced displacement has decreased for the first time in a decade, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) reported on Thursday, though the figure remains unacceptably high and tens of millions of people are still trapped in prolonged exile with little prospect of rebuilding their lives.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Haiti: Harrowing needs must be met with long-term engagement
item.description: Escalating gang violence across Haiti has pushed displacement to record levels, deepening an already severe humanitarian crisis and leaving nearly 1.5 million people without a stable place to live, according to new figures released Friday by the UN migration agency, IOM.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: UN scales up Ebola response, refugees ‘exiled’ in Africa, Political tensions escalate in Somalia
item.description: The UN and its partners are continuing efforts to contain Ebola outbreaks in both the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda, while warning that insecurity and misinformation remain major obstacles to the response.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN urges world not to forget Rohingya refugees as aid cuts threaten vital support
item.description: As the world approaches nine years since the mass displacement of Rohingya refugees from Myanmar into Bangladesh, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has appealed to the international community not to abandon the 1.2 million refugees living in the country, most of them in camps in Cox’s Bazar.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Lebanon violence continues, Israel ‘severs ties’ with UN chief, Internal displacement in Haiti, warning to France over prison overcrowding
item.description: The UN has expressed deep concern over escalating hostilities in Lebanon following intensified Israeli airstrikes in southern Beirut and across southern parts of the country.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: From Kharkiv to the UK’s health service: Ukrainian doctor rebuilds her life – and helps others do the same
item.description: On 23 February 2022, in her home city of Kharkiv, Dr Inna Soldatenko finished work, collected her daughter from school, cooked dinner and prepared a lecture for her students. The next morning, she awoke to explosions.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Star-studded refugee football team takes the pitch for UN
item.description: A symbolic team of famous footballers with first hand experience of life as a refugee was announced on Tuesday by UNHCR, just weeks ahead of the world’s biggest sporting event - the FIFA Men’s World Cup.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Countries make progress on migration pact, but more work remains
item.description: What do more than half of all doctors in Australia, over 40 per cent of Nobel laureates from the United States, and most of the workforce in some Gulf States have in common?
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Safe pathways key to reducing risk for migrants
item.description: Restricting migration does not stop people from moving. It often pushes them into more dangerous routes.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Education or food? Funding shortfalls force Sudanese refugees in Egypt to ‘make very difficult decisions’
item.description: Civilians who have fled the war in Sudan and sought shelter in neighbouring Egypt could potentially face a new battle – the loss of critical services that ensure their survival, the UN refugee agency, UNHCR, has warned.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Displacement in South Sudan, fraud centres in the Philippines, new migration patterns in Latin America
item.description: In South Sudan, the UN aid coordination office [OCHA] reported on Thursday that conflict and flooding continue to drive displacement and food insecurity higher throughout the country.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Tackling the AI digital divide, deadly migration journeys, Lucy Hale named new WFP Goodwill Ambassador
item.description: UN-led efforts are continuing to ensure that all countries can benefit and regulate Artificial Intelligence (AI) as it increasingly shapes our economies, societies and daily lives.
